commit.message:
Add session-only arguments to `/title` and `/statusline` (#54387)

## What changed

Allow inline item selection, such as `/title model reasoning` and `/statusline current-dir --no-colors`, without changing saved defaults. Support `--clear` for both commands and `--colors` or `--no-colors` for `/statusline`, including color-only updates that preserve the current items.

Carry overrides with per-thread input state across navigation and reconnects, and allow these local commands in parent-owned subagent threads. Reject invalid or conflicting arguments before applying changes. Saved editor selections supersede the corresponding overrides.

## Testing

Add coverage for argument parsing, atomic updates, rate-limit item aliases and ambiguity, thread-state restoration, saved-setting interactions, and local command submission in parent-owned threads.

GitOrigin-RevId: 909cc2ede026fbf5c7f9cd52c8cf2ae835084f14

Allow saving current permission settings as presets (#54385)

## Why

Creating a preset from current settings only offered the model. Permission presets need to preserve the profile, approval policy, and reviewer to restore the same settings.

## What changed

- Add a “Current permissions” option alongside “Current model” when creating a preset from settings.
- Extend `/permissions` with `--approval-policy` and `--reviewer`, including granular policies and quoted profile names.
- Share argument parsing between `/model` and `/permissions`, supporting quoted arguments and both `--setting=value` and `--setting value` forms.
- Keep full-access confirmation for every reviewer and reject automatic review when unavailable.

## Testing

Add parser tests, preset picker snapshots, and permission-selection tests covering complete settings restoration, invalid arguments, unavailable automatic review, and full-access confirmation.

GitOrigin-RevId: f4c9c3f6e264ee8ea4c5244c79f39f2deb15b771

Support inline permission profile selection with `/permissions` (#54383)

## What changed

Allow `/permissions <profile-id>` to select a built-in or custom permission profile, for example `/permissions :read-only`. Support `:ask-for-approval` and `:approve-for-me` aliases while preserving feature gates, profile requirements, full-access confirmation, and Windows sandbox setup.

Hold queued input until the selection is confirmed, and retain it on cancellation or failure. Reload custom profile definitions on re-selection without leaving unchanged requests pending.

## Testing

Add coverage for unknown and disabled profiles, approval aliases, confirmation and cancellation, discovery retries, Windows sandbox setup, and queued prompts waiting for server confirmation.

GitOrigin-RevId: ada38d3cfc6d6ac4e84ce5645fe33432c55d63cc

Add a keyboard shortcut menu for presets (#54381)

## What changed

Replace the `/presets` recall picker with a responsive menu above the composer. Press `0`–`9` to run a saved preset or create one in an empty slot; use `n`, `s`, `e`, and `d` to create, start from current settings, edit, and delete presets.

Add `tui.keymap.chat.open_presets` with an implicit `leader p` shortcut that yields to existing bindings and explicit configuration. Show the action in `/keymap` and add a shortcut tooltip.

Preserve the composer draft, respect popup ownership, and consume held-key repeats after menu actions.

## Testing

Add snapshots for empty, populated, and narrow preset menus, plus coverage for draft preservation, cancellation, held-key handling, transcript search precedence, and default shortcut conflicts.

GitOrigin-RevId: f438c7015dbd416c90cdeb479d2a15d9d6d24954

Add `/presets` for reusable prompts and slash commands (#54380)

## What changed

- Add a TUI picker with ten numbered preset slots, an editor, and confirmation before replacement or deletion.
- Create presets from composer text or current model, reasoning effort, and speed settings. Run saved inputs through the normal queued submission path while preserving the composer draft.
- Persist presets under `tui.presets` in the active user configuration, respecting configuration layer ownership and leaving in-memory settings unchanged when writes fail.
- Preserve permissions when changing effort or speed for the effective model, keep default collaboration settings intact in Plan mode, and allow standard-speed selection with older app servers.

## Testing

Add persistence tests for save, replace, delete, configuration ownership, and write failures; picker and confirmation snapshots; and regression coverage for model permissions and standard-speed fallback.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5f11699112cd404cc8e954872d53495c6edd0c0a

Add configuration support for TUI input presets (#54379)

## What changed

Add `tui.presets` entries keyed by a single digit from `0` to `9`, each with an `input` prompt or slash command and an optional `label`. Expose presets in the configuration schema, load them into runtime configuration, and preserve them in TUI local settings.

Reject invalid slots, blank inputs, shell commands beginning with `!` after leading whitespace, and inputs exceeding 8,000 UTF-8 bytes.

## Testing

Extend the runtime configuration test to verify loading both a slash command with a label and a prompt without one.

GitOrigin-RevId: d2911e540bc50f05b4a5224abf17ce4ef5a18ea3

Support inline model, reasoning, and speed selection in `/model` (#54378)

## What changed

Allow `/model [model] --reasoning <level> --speed <tier>` to update the current session without changing saved defaults. Both space-separated and `=` flag values are supported; omitting the model applies settings to the current model. Bare `/model` still opens the picker.

Validate model availability, supported reasoning levels, and speed tiers before applying changes. Reject unknown flags, duplicate settings, and missing values. Apply model, reasoning, and speed together after server acceptance.

Restore each thread's speed when switching threads, and use destination configuration defaults for new sessions instead of carrying over the active session's speed.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for inline commands, invalid arguments, unchanged saved defaults, settings-only updates to hidden current models, destination speed defaults, and speed restoration on the next turn after switching threads.

GitOrigin-RevId: ad9cecbdb3554e34a6518367364978a37fb68439

Retry SQLite operations on transient writer contention (#54369)

## Why

Competing SQLite writers can cause database opening and writes to fail with `SQLITE_BUSY`. Deferred write transactions can also encounter contention after taking a read snapshot.

## What changed

- Add up to two retries with 100 ms and 200 ms delays for SQLite busy errors during pool opening, writer admission, and standalone writes.
- Use a shared `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` helper across state, thread history, and agent message board writes to acquire the writer slot before reading.
- Preserve bound arguments when retrying standalone writes, and commit writes using `RETURNING` before exposing their results. Retry transaction admission without replaying an already-started transaction.

## Testing

Add tests using real SQLite writer contention to verify recovery after a competing writer releases its lock. Queue tests cover enqueue, update, and delete, checking preserved payloads, single revision increments, and no duplicate messages or unintended deletions.

GitOrigin-RevId: ac5bd31a87c67cc47fb385bf3fa5435a54ff70f0

Prevent duplicate assistant messages around interleaved commands (#54365)

## Why

When a command starts before an assistant message completes, the TUI can flush the streamed text and then render it again when the completion arrives. This duplicates the preamble in both live output and replay.

## What changed

Track the turn ID, item ID, and source text of the flushed message. Skip rendering its completion again when the identity and text match, allowing for the trailing newline added during stream finalization. Continue rendering completions whose identity or text differs.

## Testing

Add an end-to-end test that delays message completion until a command starts and checks that live and replayed transcripts contain the preamble once. Add regression coverage for completions with different text or item IDs.

GitOrigin-RevId: 59af0198a99f26ba8ba2a47644ba662301c30011

Filter uninspectable network roots from implicit MXC read grants (#54363)

## What changed

On Windows, omit network roots whose filesystem identity cannot be inspected when expanding implicit `:root` read access. Retain inspectable shares and roots containing the policy or command working directory, and apply the same filtering during policy inspection and command launch.

Keep explicit grants unchanged and continue expanding `:root` write and deny rules across all executor volumes.

## Testing

Extend policy tests to cover filtered read roots, explicit grant precedence, and approved-command write access across all volumes.

GitOrigin-RevId: c4d7c8ce2c9138cdb4518385e2cd05f66518628e

Use the turn index for turn-scoped item pagination (#54351)

## Why

A thread-wide index can scan earlier turns when a turn's final item page is underfilled.

## What changed

Force `idx_thread_items_by_turn_page` for turn-scoped item queries when neither `item_ids` nor `after_updated_at_ordinal` is set.

GitOrigin-RevId: 63c86fafa08446351a5d9828b479c497c76a8555

Add scoped executor credential auth for remote exec-server (#54346)

## What changed

- Add `RemoteEnvironmentConfig::with_executor_credential_auth()` for Noise transport, requiring exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` header without accompanying account credentials.
- Require HTTPS registry URLs except on loopback, and bypass system proxies for loopback HTTP requests.
- Mark credentials as sensitive, suppress registry diagnostics that could echo them, and reject registration responses containing the credential while preserving recognized retry error codes.
- Reject scoped executor credentials for Direct registration and WebSocket connections. Keep legacy authentication as the default.

## Testing

Add tests for invalid credential headers, HTTPS and loopback restrictions, proxy bypass, credential echoes in registry responses, and rejection before Direct transport sends requests.

GitOrigin-RevId: a427d648a0520d2e187dd40ca63268903a949f94

Centralize context fragment kind constants (#54316)

## What changed

Replace duplicated content-kind strings with constants shared by fragment producers and consumers, including authorization checks, forked-history filtering, and memory instructions. Share the compaction summary kind between core and Guardian's transcript filter.

## Testing

Add a regression test verifying that Guardian excludes compaction summaries while retaining surrounding user messages, including a user message with identical text.

GitOrigin-RevId: 36dbdf0f82c61b52d2571ac1c392fb151c98151b

Keep TUI Markdown colors readable against their backgrounds (#54315)

## Why

Syntax theme colors can have insufficient contrast against the terminal background or the shaded proposed-plan surface.

## What changed

- Adapt themed Markdown foreground colors to the terminal background while preserving inline code colors from the syntax theme.
- Adjust proposed-plan foreground colors after applying the plan background, including retained styles used for reflow. Apply the same styling to streamed and completed plans.

## Testing

Expand snapshots across syntax themes and light and dark backgrounds, and cover proposed-plan tables and streamed plans with wrapped hyperlinks. Update streaming assertions to expect contrast-adjusted blockquote colors.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0e358412562c438af17be5bcded9d058b56212b7

Enable credential masking for remote exec-server commands (#54309)

## What changed

Negotiate executor support for `credential_masking` and enable built-in credential brokerage in executor-local network proxies. Supported non-login Bash commands on Linux and macOS receive credential placeholders, with real credentials injected by the proxy for matching destinations.

Retain credential mappings across process launches within the same executor session, scoped by environment, conversation, and broker configuration. Keep credentials and destination context on the executor.

Fall back to unmasked execution for unsupported shells or shell startup, and for configured credential providers. Emit warnings when masking is unavailable, preserving shell profiles and snapshots.

## Testing

Add coverage for capability negotiation, fallback behavior, mapping reuse and isolation, proxy credential injection, and keeping executor credentials out of model-visible request history. Test warning, removal, and rejection modes for credentials left unmasked during preparation.

GitOrigin-RevId: f64e916a5de8350fa0d289d3440ec29761accd75

Attribute compaction summaries to the assistant in Guardian transcripts (#54281)

## Why

Local compaction stores generated summaries with the `user` wire role, but those summaries are not user authorization. Guardian transcripts need to preserve that distinction when reviewing compacted history.

## What changed

Classify messages marked with `compaction.summary` as assistant entries in Guardian transcripts, while preserving the attribution of actual user messages.

## Testing

Add transcript collection coverage and regression tests for both line and JSON transcripts that verify generated summaries are attributed to the assistant and original user instructions remain attributed to the user.

GitOrigin-RevId: 66183028ce70a2500d47d3347b110f95471ba868

Share Guardian image deduplication and checkpoint restoration (#54278)

## What changed

- Add `ComposedContext::retain_new_images` and use it in Guardian review sessions and the async scorer. Compare host-prepared image references against admitted history, ignoring image detail, and skip scanning history when no images need checking.
- Restore `ConversationState` directly from a checkpoint, retaining committed history for rollback or transferring it with `take_history` for ephemeral forks.

## Testing

Extend tests for prepared-image matching across differing detail levels, image-free continuations that avoid scanning history, and checkpoint restoration and history transfer.

GitOrigin-RevId: bafeb6de9babc721182be43d0eb1a653955a0ebb

Protect metadata writes through macOS case aliases (#54273)

## Why

On case-insensitive macOS filesystems, paths such as `.GIT/config` refer to protected `.git/config` metadata but can pass case-sensitive write permission checks.

## What changed

Check native filesystem case sensitivity when matching protected metadata paths, including case aliases in workspace roots. Recheck both the target and policy entries with normalized aliases so explicit metadata grants and narrower restrictions retain their precedence. Return errors when filesystem case sensitivity cannot be established.

## Testing

Add macOS coverage for metadata and workspace-root case aliases, explicit grants, narrower restrictions, and missing directories. Strengthen the patch regression test to assert the approval rejection message for both direct `apply_patch` calls and shell interception.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8ae2eb97ce6ec71c51bead130515b9ce6c1cdfab

Add regression coverage for Guardian sandbox retry approvals (#54265)

## What changed

Add an integration test that approves a sandboxed `exec_command` attempt, simulates a sandbox denial, and denies the subsequent unsandboxed retry. Verify that Guardian reviews the retry separately with `require_escalated`, that the denied retry never reaches the executor, and that the tool result includes the denial rationale.

Use a fake executor to exercise the sandbox denial consistently across hosts.

GitOrigin-RevId: cd644255f7a7b7561c9e52a5b6e40f0859b70547

Track Guardian transcript admission across failed reviews (#54264)

## Why

A failed Guardian inference can retain its input in a reusable session. Tracking transcript progress only after successful reviews can admit the same evidence again on retry.

## What changed

Advance transcript progress when a failed turn has retained its input and the session remains reusable, without counting it as a completed review or changing the committed fork checkpoint. Leave progress unchanged when failure occurs before input admission.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for encrypted agent messages across review retries, pending evidence after compaction failures, and fork checkpoints after transcript admission without a completed review.

GitOrigin-RevId: 36239ec9d47f484bcfe68d65e7c8d8ab8660db0d

Require fresh Guardian approval for escalated tool retries (#54263)

## Why

Guardian approval covers the permissions of the reviewed action. A retry outside the sandbox needs a fresh review of its broader permissions.

## What changed

- Track the initial approval source so Guardian approval does not preapprove an escalated retry, while preserving existing user and hook approval behavior.
- For exec retries that can run without the sandbox, set the approval action to `RequireEscalated` and clear `additional_permissions` so review and caching reflect the retry's actual permissions.

GitOrigin-RevId: 06f8d53745a7bcfe9fdb5628ff9e85da6060547d

Preserve recent speech when trimming realtime transcripts (#54257)

## Why

Trimming interleaved realtime transcripts by utterance order can discard the latest speech from an earlier utterance. Evicting after each delta can also drop one speaker before the other speaker's delta from the same frame arrives, losing recent instructions at handoff.

## What changed

Use raw frame recency to trim timed frameless bidirectional transcripts within the 8 KiB budget. Defer eviction until the frame advances or the transcript is consumed, and retain both speakers' suffixes when they share the newest frame. Preserve conversation order and fall back to FIFO eviction when timing is unavailable.

Track trimmed prefixes so final transcripts can extend retained speech without making delayed finals appear newer.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for frame recency, same-frame event ordering, UTF-8 truncation, delayed finals, and untimed fallback. Add an app-server handoff test verifying that both speakers' recent speech and the latest user instruction survive while live transcript notifications remain unchanged.

GitOrigin-RevId: b01b729d8bdd4acb26e0385442ce40819355deac

Add regression tests for case-variant metadata protection (#54250)

## What changed

- Verify that freeform `apply_patch` calls and shell-intercepted patches cannot modify `.git/config` through `.GIT/config` when approvals are disabled, while an ordinary workspace file remains writable.
- Add macOS Seatbelt coverage for uppercase protected metadata paths, including absent directories, existing directories with either casing, and case variants of the workspace root. Assert that metadata creation and modification are denied while sibling workspace writes succeed.

The tests skip filesystems that do not support the case-insensitive aliases they exercise.

GitOrigin-RevId: 5cf6b0c36eee348e1ba0db0bc2d3bff072458364

Apply syntax theme colors to Markdown prose in the TUI (#54217)

## What changed

Use the active syntax theme's markup foregrounds for headings, emphasis, strong text, list markers, links, and blockquotes. Preserve existing bold, italic, and underline modifiers, and retain previous styles when a scope provides no foreground.

## Testing

Update rendering snapshots and streaming blockquote assertions for themed colors. Exercise existing fallback expectations with an empty syntax theme.

GitOrigin-RevId: b00aa4af30f73f538ff5f888a0f9b4edbdc15893

Show image previews in the fullscreen transcript (#54216)

## What changed

Render local viewed images and generated image artifacts as bounded thumbnails in the rich fullscreen transcript using Kitty or Sixel graphics. Viewed images appear when their activity is expanded or the detailed presentation is active; generated images appear alongside their saved-path entry.

Keep previews clipped to the viewport, retain graphics across unrelated redraws, and remove them when overlays open. Bound image decoding and cache memory, and preserve text-only entries for remote workspaces, unsupported terminals, missing files, and oversized images. Image rows do not enter searchable or selectable text.

## Testing

Add layout and snapshot coverage for disclosure, viewport clipping, rewrapping, raw-mode fallback, deleted files, and oversized rasters. Add terminal coverage for retained Kitty graphics, repainting after a clear, local-file transport, and overlay cleanup.

GitOrigin-RevId: fb2ec146331acfcfc82b2b283616671c9ee93757

Retire worktree and voice feature flags (#54175)

## What changed

- Remove feature-flag checks from managed worktree creation and repository-aware session discovery, while retaining local workspace and trust checks.
- Make TUI voice availability follow platform support instead of `features.realtime_conversation`.
- Ignore `features.worktrees` and `features.realtime_conversation` configuration overrides, warn when managed requirements reference them, and hide both flags from `/experimental`, including catalogs from older servers.

## Testing

Add coverage for ignored configuration overrides and managed requirements, and update session filtering, worktree grouping, and experimental feature discovery tests for the retired flags.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1d64e890e6e2f8a78926a9ea163126c0890b068e

Preserve ChatGPT authentication for Gov MCP servers (#54170)

## Why

MCP servers at `https://gov.chatgpt.com` were treated as untrusted for ChatGPT authentication and switched to OAuth, preventing local Gov Apps from retaining the ChatGPT auth provider.

## What changed

Trust the `https://gov.chatgpt.com` origin alongside the existing ChatGPT origin when resolving MCP server authentication. Origin matching preserves scheme, host, and port restrictions.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for Gov Apps URL construction, trusted origin normalization, rejection of lookalike hosts and nonstandard schemes or ports, and retention of the local ChatGPT auth provider. Verify that explicit OAuth servers and servers in remote environments do not receive the host provider.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7ceaf7c524d963005d9f23204489bbde269f0dd5

Reload the model catalog after account changes (#54169)

## Why

The app server retained its startup model provider for catalog requests, so signing in or out could leave `model/list` using stale provider settings or requiring a restart after managed provider requirements changed.

## What changed

- Invalidate the catalog after successful login and logout, then reload the effective configuration on the next model list or background refresh. Rebuild the models manager when the provider or catalog changes, while preserving existing threads' routes.
- Retain the original project context and the TUI's `--oss` provider selection across reloads. Retry configuration loading after falling back to defaults so temporary failures do not pin the fallback catalog.
- Keep provider policy checks for cached catalogs and apply runtime `api_key_model_discovery` toggles to the active catalog manager.

## Testing

Add and extend tests for provider selection and definition changes after login, catalog reloads after logout, OAuth gateway transitions, fallback recovery, project context, and runtime model discovery toggles.

GitOrigin-RevId: bce2e23ff567e1a52eac2b6ad736a6e63ff61e2b

Generate keymap descriptors and binding accessors from one catalog (#54151)

## Why

The `/keymap` action catalog and root-config binding lookup duplicated the same action inventory, requiring both to be maintained together.

## What changed

Use `define_keymap_actions!` to generate `KEYMAP_ACTIONS` and `binding_slot` from a single declaration grouped by context. Preserve the existing action order, descriptions, feature gates, and binding mappings.

GitOrigin-RevId: 182e937d9642a8b5a4aa787691da793712f29010

Allow large file writes over direct exec-server WebSockets (#54135)

## Why

Direct mode serves executor requests but applied the client's 8 KiB inbound request limit, causing larger `fs/writeFile` requests to disconnect the executor.

## What changed

Use a dedicated direct WebSocket connection constructor that omits the client inbound request limit while retaining WebSocket message and frame limits.

## Testing

Add a regression test that runs the direct environment and verifies successful file writes above the client request limit using both text and binary WebSocket messages.

GitOrigin-RevId: e8e77a5e8581ab9eb98446e23b77a6da41d64868

Record per-tool incremental update and description size metrics (#54133)

## What changed

Tag `codex.tools.incremental_updates` counters with the qualified tool name alongside the action. Continue excluding initial catalogs and namespace headers, while counting each removed namespace member.

Add `codex.tools.spec_description_bytes` to measure UTF-8 description bytes when an existing tool definition is replaced. Skip definitions without descriptions and use logarithmic histogram boundaries up to 1 MiB.

## Testing

Extend namespace transition tests to check per-tool counts and description sizes. Add scenario assertions for replacement metrics with incremental tool updates and their absence on the non-incremental request path.

GitOrigin-RevId: e20e6d81f21a867b285df1f0da005c2806dd03c6

Allow stdin review under active grants with sandbox prompts disabled (#54119)

## Why

With granular sandbox approvals disabled, `write_stdin` rejected input to terminals retaining additional permissions even when those permissions were still granted.

## What changed

Let input reach approval review when the terminal's retained permissions match active grants for its environment. Require identical filesystem grants, including entry order, and an active network grant when retained permissions enable network access. Each input still requires review.

Keep rejecting input when retained authority is no longer covered or the approval policy changes to `Never`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for user and Guardian review, turn grant expiry, session grants, and switching to `Never`. Cover filesystem restrictions, protected metadata, symlinks, and ordered denials, and verify that rejected input never reaches the terminal.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9abf7da8d03b1526d26ca2a718e36349a255330b

Report terminal completion states and blocking reasons (#54114)

## Why

Terminal status previously collapsed completed and failed turns into `idle` and reported blocking prompts without a reason. Blocking detection also depended on terminal title settings.

## What changed

- Emit `done` and `error` through OSC 7501 for live turn results, retaining them until deliberate keyboard, paste, or mouse input acknowledges them. Mouse movement does not acknowledge results.
- Classify blocking requests with `kind=permission`, `kind=question`, or `kind=auth`, including requests hidden behind another view or delayed while typing, independently of terminal title settings.
- Keep pending follow-up work and active goals `working`. Treat interrupted turns and replayed results as `idle` rather than new results.
- Preserve the existing iTerm2 OSC 21337 labels and indicators, mapping `done` and `error` to `Idle`.

## Testing

Add lifecycle and input-acknowledgment tests covering approvals, completion, failure, interruption, replay, pending follow-ups, and active goals. Extend blocking-request assertions and terminal protocol snapshots for the new states and reasons.

GitOrigin-RevId: 90bad1d54d8b3b9e3cec66fbd3bf3df0c42b995b

Embed generated app-server schema bundles in Bazel builds (#54113)

## What changed

Use the stable and experimental bundles generated by `//bazel/schema:app-server` as compile-time inputs for `app-server-protocol` instead of the checked-in bundles.

Generalize `schema_generator_sources` to `schema_sources` so it can stage Rust sources alongside generated bundles. Keep empty bundle placeholders for the on-demand schema generator, which derives its output from Rust sources.

GitOrigin-RevId: a976c420a3698d631f3ea7c698b15b82391158e5

Wait for readiness in the SIGTERM cancellation test (#54099)

## What changed

Wait for the subprocess readiness marker before cancelling in
`process_exec_tool_call_cancellation_allows_sigterm_cleanup`, removing the
one-second polling cutoff. Poll readiness alongside execution under the existing
five-second timeout, then cancel and await execution if that timeout expires so
cleanup completes before the test fails.

GitOrigin-RevId: ba47dad9ba87fb5dc3bd087380811655387f825a

Keep environment tools stable across readiness changes (#54098)

## Why

Environment tool availability and selectors should remain stable as selected environments become ready.

## What changed

- Keep configured environment tools advertised even when no execution environment is ready, and derive `environment_id` selectors from all selected environments.
- Return guidance to wait when an environment is unavailable, while preserving errors for unknown environment IDs. Require a usable primary environment for `write_stdin`.
- Always include `shell` and `login` in the `exec_command` schema and mark `stable_environment_tools` as removed.

## Testing

Update integration tests to expect environment tools with empty or starting environments, and remove explicit feature opt-ins from affected scenarios.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1590c1b5be16a39e4a370663c552b881602545b5

Show Daybreak notices after the session header (#54097)

## What changed

Emit the Daybreak notice after replacing or removing the placeholder session header so the notice follows the configured header.

## Testing

Extend the resumed-history snapshot test to start with a placeholder header and verify the full transcript order: session header, Daybreak notice, and replayed user and assistant messages.

GitOrigin-RevId: 536f717b2859d2fe319756f52123b4cd0407cb66

Add Bazel targets for on-demand schemas and Python SDK generation (#54096)

## What changed

- Add `//bazel/schema:app-server` to generate stable and experimental schemas from Rust sources without depending on committed precomputed bundles.
- Add `//sdk/python:generated` to generate Python SDK models, the notification registry, and API methods from the stable schema in scratch space, using dependencies from `uv.lock`.
- Add `generate-types --no-format` to skip formatters for build outputs while preserving formatting by default.

## Testing

Extend contract generation tests to regenerate in a temporary SDK copy, checking byte equality for formatted output and AST equality for unformatted output.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9ca7daa8ac0a33c4106a9e95c2f48bbded07df21

Preserve specific MCP failure codes in metrics and spans (#54094)

## Why

MCP request failures and tool errors reported only through `codex/telemetry` metadata previously received an `unknown` error code, obscuring the failure category.

## What changed

- Classify typed request failures into bounded codes such as `request_timeout`, `transport_closed`, and `protocol_error`, and carry them into MCP call metrics and spans before errors become strings.
- Preserve typed timeouts when a prepared tool call exhausts its deadline during trusted access lookup.
- Accept allowlisted `error_code` values from `codex/telemetry` as a fallback after structured content and connector authentication metadata. Keep model output unchanged and ignore unrecognized metadata codes.

## Testing

Add coverage for typed errors wrapped in context, prepared-call timeout classification, metadata precedence and rejection, unchanged model output, and exported span error attributes.

GitOrigin-RevId: d7a440a6c9119b8a07a7f1fad697eb25af506f00

Upgrade Bazel's `rules_python` to 2.4.2 (#54087)

## What changed

- Upgrade `rules_python` from 1.7.0 to 2.4.2 and update `MODULE.bazel.lock`.
- Enable `--windows_enable_symlinks` in `.bazelrc`, as `rules_python` 2.x requires symlink support for Windows Python launchers.

GitOrigin-RevId: 303da258c74b18d0d0df8d4eebb830c57f14cca4

Stabilize the Guardian network review timeout test (#54082)

## Why

Advancing the test clock expires the review, but command cancellation and output drainage still run asynchronously. The model can poll before the final timeout failure is available.

## What changed

Hold the initial tool result until the command emits `ExecCommandEnd`, with a bounded wait that also catches unexpected approval requests or turn completion. Only request a poll when the initial result reports a running process, and accept the timeout output from either `exec_command` or `write_stdin`.

Keep the assertions that the model receives the timeout explanation without a user approval prompt or a misleading user-rejection message.

GitOrigin-RevId: 219a1579dce35caf8f0d45b1d92a7343ec1a8935

Centralize vertical navigation in TUI list views (#54081)

## What changed

Add `ListKeymap::vertical_action_for` and `ScrollState::apply_vertical_action` to share key resolution, selection movement, and visibility handling across the experimental features, hooks, memories, skills, and multi-select views. Preserve navigation priority, search input handling, and item reordering precedence.

## Testing

Update scroll-state tests to exercise the shared action handler and picker tests to navigate through key events. Cover overlapping page-down and move-left bindings when item reordering is disabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: 29927b0a4de0fbeb4c0dd19c418b8f60fffb8a7d

Extract TUI user-turn submission into a dedicated module (#54080)

## What changed

Move `AppCommand::UserTurn` handling from `thread_routing.rs` into
`user_turn_submission.rs`. Keep turn creation, permission resolution, and
active-turn steering behavior together, preserving retry and queueing behavior.

Avoid false URL-launch detections in literal PowerShell commands (#54076)

Unarchiving a thread previously read rollout metadata across both active and archived history, including unrelated threads.

Support store-owned preparation when resuming threads (#54059)

Thread stores need a way to reuse history and writer state loaded while preparing a resume, rather than loading them again during session startup.

Forward turn metadata to image generation and edit requests (#54058)

Use the Responses metadata template for native extension calls while continuing to exclude tool inventory. Forward the resulting metadata in the `x-codex-turn-metadata` header on image generation and edit requests.

Extend metadata tests to cover configured values in extension calls and app-server tests to verify `display_name` and `turn_trigger` on image generation and edit requests, including a Unicode display name.

GitOrigin-RevId: a2ffaa4d15259c662917612391b8717ee34b9c6c

Distinguish unsupported evidence in Decisions comparison metrics (#54057)

## Why

Unsupported evidence currently shares a single Decisions comparison reason, making it difficult to distinguish why a comparison was skipped.

## What changed

Report separate reasons for unsupported developer messages, other non-user messages, trusted skills, images, and audio. Keep these outcomes classified as `skipped` and retain the generic reason for other unsupported evidence. Expose `TrustedSkills::KIND` for identifying trusted skill fragments.

## Testing

Expand adapter tests for the distinct rejection reasons and add a lifecycle case verifying that trusted skill evidence skips the Decisions request, reports `trusted_skills`, and preserves the baseline score.

GitOrigin-RevId: 98f076d1aa6771d0209e7f5910eed0dcc40c6263

Coalesce overlapping native TLS root certificate loads (#54056)

## Why

Concurrent TLS client builds can independently load the same platform trust store. Share overlapping loads while preserving fresh trust reads for later builds.

- Bypass sharing when `SSL_CERT_FILE` or `SSL_CERT_DIR` is set, and continue reading custom CA bundles independently for every build.

## Testing

Add tests for overlapping loads, fresh trust after completion, and recovery from a panicking loader. Extend TLS handshake coverage to verify that replacing a custom CA file affects new configurations while existing configurations retain their trust, and that empty or removed files produce errors.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1465ef3faf82f53651d9dbfe314341b17346580b

Add Responses API client metadata patches for turn start and steer (#54053)

## Why

Clients need a way to update individual turn metadata entries without replacing the existing client metadata map.

Continue protecting reserved metadata keys and preserving targeted `misalignment_override` continuations across updates.

Extend the app-server metadata integration test to cover replacement and patch steering, patch precedence at turn start, preservation of unrelated entries during patches, and protection of targeted continuations.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8c4da3ba1b87329da20b5295846bdcf3a88126de

Scope TUI skill refreshes and workspace commands to explicit directories (#54050)

A queued skill refresh can outlive the workspace it was requested for when the working directory changes.

- Require an explicit working directory when constructing `WorkspaceCommand` and always pass it to app-server command execution. Update Git and GitHub metadata probes to use the constructor.

Extend regression tests to verify that closing skill management refreshes the configured working directory and that stale skill refreshes after a directory change do not issue a `skills/list` request.

GitOrigin-RevId: 47ad1d95930840b3f6f0e20d7d8fe8d025e789e6

Defer folder trust checks until starting a task from agents overview (#54048)

## Why

The Agent Command Center does not open a workspace, so viewing it should not require consent for the launch directory.

Skip startup folder consent when opening the agents overview, while preserving initialization for the embedded fallback. Check folder trust before starting the first task, including through `/new` after dismissing the overview. On Windows, retain the sandbox setup prompt after folder trust is granted.

## Testing

Add CLI tests for starting a task from an untrusted folder through the overview and through `/new` after dismissing it. A terminal snapshot verifies that the overview appears before folder consent.

GitOrigin-RevId: 129be14a354b8abde2e8430c81599e2064ccac87

Restore elapsed time for replayed in-progress turns (#54047)

Replaying an in-progress turn reset the TUI's `Working` timer to zero, hiding time already spent on the turn.

Initialize the status timer from the turn's `started_at` timestamp when replaying turns or turn-start notifications. Keep the zero-time fallback when the timestamp is missing, and clamp future timestamps to zero elapsed time.

## Testing

Extend history replay tests to verify elapsed time for both thread snapshots and replayed in-progress turns, and normalize the timer in rendering snapshots.

GitOrigin-RevId: 36a48f43d0d7aa530f1bfe6dbefa9f0885cbd6c7

Track approval cancellation sources and Guardian context changes (#54046)

## What changed

- Record `context_changed` when validating a Guardian allow against changed authorization or review context, even when a concurrent stop or history reset determines the outcome. Retain the flag across retries and fresh-checkpoint recovery, and include it in the Guardian review counter.

GitOrigin-RevId: a19a986a7565f9a78a9bb2eaabdb5651834d28b8

Keep fork lineage ahead of paginated transcript history (#54044)

Add regression tests for repeated history prepends in both paths, verifying that fork lineage stays first.

GitOrigin-RevId: 71497fb7ffa992c72ee08617d318aa3119e71275

Return async Guardian approvals before review cleanup finishes (#54039)

An asynchronous approval currently waits for the redundant synchronous review to finish cancellation cleanup before returning a decision.

Cancel the redundant review and let it drain under the parent's `ReviewerTasks` tracker so a current approval can return immediately. Revalidate the approval and check cancellation before approving the action. Hosts without a task tracker continue to wait for cleanup.

Add tests covering current, invalidated, and cancelled approvals while cleanup is blocked, suppression of late evidence, reviewer reservations during cleanup, and shutdown waiting for abandoned attempts.

Bound concurrent Git diffs for untracked files (#54032)

## Why

Collecting a diff previously launched a Git process for every untracked file at once, allowing process counts to grow with the number of files.

Limit untracked-file diffs to eight concurrent operations per collection while preserving patch order and skipping failed file diffs. Concurrent collections each retain their own limit.

Add tests for independent concurrency limits, failed-file handling, and patch order and application with tracked changes, binary files, and filenames containing spaces or a leading dash.

GitOrigin-RevId: 896e896eae62ba9b7acf3e8946c235fe725ced40

Preserve Windows startup variables and MXC child environment defaults (#54027)

Fix session lookup and resume after rollout compression (#54008)

Compression replaces `.jsonl` rollout files with `.jsonl.zst` files, so checking only the original path can skip existing sessions. Compression can also replace a file between path lookup and canonicalization.

Extend coverage to verify latest-session filtering after startup compression and resuming a compressed rollout through its original relative `.jsonl` path with preserved turns.

Extend the rollout statistics test to cover nested plain and compressed files, coexisting representations, archived compressed rollouts, and ignored files, with a snapshot of the reported counts and sizes.

Apply the thread or rollout ID filter before resolving plain/compressed file precedence. Preserve preference for uncompressed files and selection of the newest rollout for a thread.

Extend lookup tests to cover unrelated compressed files, uncompressed-file precedence, missing rollout IDs, and rollout ID tie-breaking for files with the same timestamp.

Update archive and delete progress tests and snapshots to cover navigation, resize handling, immediate task hiding, and suppression of task switching and creation while requests are pending.

GitOrigin-RevId: eeca69067b4d9cd91c817732d79b4d5c1faa18b9

Extend coverage for stale selection history, retention of the last two selections, packages containing external symlinks, partial deletion and reinstall, cleanup without restarting the daemon, and repeated installs preserving selection history.

Retain rollout migration locks across worker cancellation (#53794)

## Why

Cancelling an async migration caller can leave its blocking compression or decompression worker running. Releasing migration locks before that worker finishes allows other writers or migrations to access files still being processed.

## What changed

Share maintenance, cross-process writer, and local writer locks with blocking workers during migration and recovery. Keep those locks held until file work completes, releasing cross-process locks before allowing local writers to proceed.

## Testing

Add a regression test for cancelled compression and decompression callers that verifies locks remain held until the worker finishes and the output is complete. Preserve the Unix check that decompression temporaries have owner-only permissions.

Fix cancellation of macOS user-verification prompts (#53790)

## Why

Keychain signing reconstructs its own authentication context, so invalidating the caller's context does not reliably cancel the context that owns the biometric prompt.

## What changed

Evaluate the stored key's access-control policy explicitly with `LAContext` before signing. On cancellation, invalidate that context and wait for its authorization callback before releasing the lifecycle lock, rejecting any late success. Reload the key with the authorized context and disable further interaction so signing cannot open another prompt.

## Testing

Update unit tests to cover waiting for cancellation completion and rejecting completed authorization after cancellation. Add an ignored macOS hardware test and setup instructions covering persisted Secure Enclave key reuse, signature verification, cancellation, retry signing, and cleanup.
